proof_nl: Let v_i := phi(u_i) for i = 1,...,n. For each i = 0,...,n, set I_i := (u_1,...,u_i) and J_i := (v_1,...,v_i), with I_0 = J_0 = (0). Because phi is an algebra automorphism, phi(I_i) = J_i for every i. Hence phi induces an isomorphism of quotient rings bar_phi_i : A / I_i -> A / J_i, given by a + I_i |-> phi(a) + J_i; its inverse is induced by phi^{-1}. Now let u_i have degree d. Since phi is a graded automorphism, it preserves each graded piece, so phi(u_i) also lies in the degree-d piece. Therefore deg(phi(u_i)) = d = deg(u_i) for every i. It remains to prove preservation of regular sequences. Use the standard ring-theoretic definition: a sequence x_1,...,x_n is regular if for each i >= 1, the class of x_i is a non-zero-divisor in A / (x_1,...,x_{i-1}); if one also adopts the common extra condition that the final quotient A / (x_1,...,x_n) be nonzero, that condition is also preserved here because the final quotients are isomorphic. Assume first that u_1,...,u_n is a regular sequence. Fix i with 1 <= i <= n. Suppose that in A / J_{i-1} one has (v_i + J_{i-1})(a + J_{i-1}) = 0. Then v_i a is in J_{i-1} = phi(I_{i-1}). Applying phi^{-1}, we get u_i phi^{-1}(a) in I_{i-1}. Equivalently, in A / I_{i-1} we have (u_i + I_{i-1})(phi^{-1}(a) + I_{i-1}) = 0. Since u_i + I_{i-1} is a non-zero-divisor in A / I_{i-1}, it follows that phi^{-1}(a) + I_{i-1} = 0, so phi^{-1}(a) is in I_{i-1}. Applying phi, we obtain a in J_{i-1}. Thus v_i + J_{i-1} is a non-zero-divisor in A / J_{i-1}. Since this holds for every i, the sequence v_1,...,v_n is regular. If one includes the additional condition A / I_n != 0 in the definition, it is preserved as well because bar_phi_n is an isomorphism A / I_n ~= A / J_n. Conversely, if v_1,...,v_n is regular, the same argument applied to the automorphism phi^{-1} shows that u_1,...,u_n is regular. Therefore u_1,...,u_n is a regular sequence if and only if phi(u_1),...,phi(u_n) is a regular sequence. Together with the degree argument above, this proves the lemma.

domain_restrictions: A must be a graded commutative algebra over the rational numbers
phi must be an automorphism of A that preserves the grading and the Q-algebra structure
each u_i must be homogeneous in A
the sequence length is finite and indexed by integers from 1 to n
regular sequence is interpreted in the commutative algebra underlying A
semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For every graded commutative Q-algebra A, every grading-preserving Q-algebra automorphism phi of A, every finite sequence of homogeneous elements u_1 through u_n in A, the sequence u_1 through u_n is a regular sequence exactly when the image sequence phi(u_1) through phi(u_n) is a regular sequence; in addition, phi preserves the degree of each sequence element.
quantifier_order: for every graded commutative Q-algebra A
for every graded Q-algebra automorphism phi of A
for every choice of homogeneous elements u_1 through u_n in A
for each index i from 1 to n

variables.domain: algebras over the rational numbers equipped with a grading
variables.name: A

variables.domain: self-maps of A that are algebra automorphisms, Q-linear, and grading-preserving
variables.name: phi

variables.domain: elements of A with a well-defined degree
variables.name: u_i

witness_dependencies: There are no existential witnesses in the statement; it is a universal preservation claim.
The degree comparison is pointwise for each index i and does not depend on any additional choice.

statement_nl: Let A be a graded commutative Q-algebra, let phi : A -> A be a graded Q-algebra automorphism, and let u_1,...,u_n be homogeneous elements of A. Then u_1,...,u_n is a regular sequence if and only if phi(u_1),...,phi(u_n) is a regular sequence. Moreover deg(phi(u_i)) = deg(u_i) for every i.
